To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the competitive structure of the higher education industry is characterized by a small number of large firms, a large number of small firms, and a few firms of medium size; (2) the number of firms in the industry has been increasing at a rapid rate; (3) the number of mergers and acquisitions has been increasing rapidly; and (4) the number of students enrolled in the industry has increased at an increasing rate.

(1) The number of students enrolled in private nonprofit colleges is declining, while the number of students enrolled at for-profits and public institutions is growing; and (2) the number of students attending public institutions has grown faster than the number of students at private nonprofit institutions, while the number attending for-profit institutions has grown faster …

(1) the distribution of students among institutions is changing in a way that is not consistent with a competitive structure; (2) the distribution of institutions is not changing; and (3) the distribution of resources among institutions is not changing.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the distribution of students among institutions of higher education and the implications of that distribution.
the competitive structure of the higher education market.
the distribution of students among institutions of higher education, with particular reference to the public and private sectors.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there is a great deal of diversity among the various institutions in the United States and that this diversity has been increasing in recent years.
there are no simple answers to the question, "What are the competitive structures in higher education?"
there is not enough data available to make a conclusive statement.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we are not in favor of any of the three models of competition.
the competitive structure of higher education is characterized by a large number of institutions with a small number of very large institutions.
we are in the midst of a major transformation in higher education.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there are many different ways to measure competition in higher education and the results can differ substantially depending on how you measure it.
the structure of higher education is changing.
the structure of the higher education system is not a static one.
